title: The MCP Context Problem and the Network Fix
summary: MCP gives AI workflows a standardized way to access enterprise systems, but agents still lack operational context. NETSCOUT bridges this gap with semantically rich Smart Data.
body_markdown:
Almost everyone building agentic workflows started out looking for the same thing: seamless integration. Model Context Protocol (MCP) solves the connection problem. But what about the context problem?


MCP gives AI assistants and AI agents a standardized way to access enterprise systems. That’s a significant step forward. In IT operations, however, access alone doesn’t guarantee the operational context AI needs to understand what’s happening across connected systems.


Have we just kicked the can further down the road?


When an AI agent investigates an application slowdown, it might invoke MCP tools to fetch metrics from a monitoring system or logs from a security information and event management (SIEM) platform, only to find that neither explains the problem. Each query takes time and consumes tokens. The missing link may be a service dependency neither system captures.


In its recent report “[AI-Ready Data Isn’t New—It’s the Unfinished Work of Enterprise Data Management](https://www.forrester.com/report/ai-ready-data-isnt-new-its-the-unfinished-work-of-enterprise-data-management/RES195007) ,” Forrester identifies a lack of context, structure, and meaningful relationships in enterprise data as barriers to accurate, reliable AI outcomes.


That’s what everyone was really looking for all along.


## When Connected Tools Deliver More Data Than AI Needs


New techniques such as[deferred tool loading](https://www.anthropic.com/research/advanced-tool-use) may reduce the context consumed by MCP tool definitions so AI assistants powered by large language models (LLMs) can discover tools as needed. But what happens when a tool returns far more information than the investigation requires?


A query might produce an oversized JSON response containing thousands of lines of telemetry, causing useful evidence to be buried under unrelated metrics. So the assistant queries another system, then another. Tokens accumulate, time passes, and the original question is still not answered.


AI needs evidence that explains exactly what’s happening, not mountains of telemetry to dig through.


## Better Context Starts Before the AI Asks


Network traffic captures how applications and services communicate, including interactions and dependencies that other data sources may miss.


[NETSCOUT](https://www.netscout.com/) uses deep packet inspection (DPI) at scale and Adaptive Service Intelligence (ASI) to perform early semantic extraction. This process captures[operational meaning at the point of observation](https://www.netscout.com/observability) and delivers it as structured, high-cardinality Smart Data so AI workflows can:


· Use[response times and protocol behavior](https://www.netscout.com/resources/case-studies/top-healthcare-insurer-improves-enterprise-wide-service-performance-with-netscout-visibility) to identify where application performance is deteriorating


· Examine[network-derived dependencies](https://www.netscout.com/resources/case-studies/netscout-pinpoints-source-of-months-long-slowdown-in-custom-payment-gateway-app) to understand how services interact and where problems may have a wider impact


· Query[specific Smart Data via MCP](https://www.netscout.com/resources/solution-briefs/overview-similar-embed-opening-the-ai-black-box-with-netscouts-mcp-server) based on the investigation


For example, let’s say a sales rep notices that customer records in their CRM platform are taking an unusually long time to open. Other CRM functions, such as contact searches and lead tracking, seem fine, so IT focuses on the laggy records. But an AI assistant querying Smart Data finds that the slow transactions share a dependency on an external customer verification service. The CRM system isn’t necessarily the source of the trouble. It’s waiting on something else.


That discovery changes the investigation. Instead of pulling more CRM metrics, the assistant can correlate affected transactions with the external service’s response times and focus on the dependency that may be causing the delay.


Rather than reconstructing relationships from scattered telemetry, the assistant can retrieve focused evidence via MCP and compare it with information from other systems. For AIOps, AgenticOps, and others, that means faster access to meaningful evidence, more grounded analysis with less risk of hallucination, and reduced token consumption.


## NETSCOUT Brings Network Intelligence to MCP


[NETSCOUT’s Omnis AI Insights](https://www.netscout.com/solutions/aiops-enterprise) makes network-derived Smart Data available to AI assistants and agents through[Omnis Streamer’s built-in MCP server](https://www.netscout.com/blog/introducing-omnis-streamers-built-mcp-server-netscouts-latest) . During investigations, they can query relevant application and service intelligence on demand to bring deep operational context into existing workflows to support more informed reasoning. In this way, IT teams spend less time chasing false positives or pursuing the wrong root cause and can more confidently evaluate what the evidence reveals.


To put it simply: MCP makes the connection.[NETSCOUT Smart Data](https://www.netscout.com/resources/rc/col/top/overview-similar-embed-opening-the-ai-black-box-with-netscouts-mcp-server) gives that connection meaning.
